name: Malluch
overview: Malluch was a male descendant of Bani who is noted in Scripture for having married a foreign wife, as recorded in Ezra 10:29. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, he is mentioned among those who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah 10:27. His inclusion in these texts highlights his role in the post-exilic community's efforts to renew their commitment to God's law.
namesAndTitles: The name Malluch is a proper name meaning 'counselor; king' according to Ezra 10:29. This name does not appear to have been given directly by God but reflects a title that conveys leadership or wisdom.
familyAndRelationships: Malluch is explicitly identified as a descendant of Bani, establishing a direct familial connection. Beyond this, Scripture does not record any additional family relationships for him apart from his noted marriage to a foreign wife.
scriptureSignificance: Malluch's significance lies in his representation of the challenges faced by the post-exilic community in maintaining covenant purity, as he was among those who had intermarried with foreign women. His presence on the sealed document in Nehemiah 10:27 underscores his participation in the communal recommitment to God's law, reflecting the broader movement to restore Israel's faithfulness after the exile.
